text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The statistical bureau expects the purchasing power of the "average Slovak citizen" to reach 1989 levels this year.
- The income of Slovak families rose 16 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters of this year and totalled about 336 billion crowns.

- Overall investment in the wood processing industry, including paper and cellulose production, will total some 16.5 billion crowns over the next four years. Around 12.7 billion crowns should come from foreign credits, 2.09 billion should be covered by domestic loans and 1.75 billion will come from the industry's own resources.

- The Russian-Slovak joint-venture tyre maker Matador Omskshina, in which Slovakia's sole tyre producer Matador Puchov holds 50 percent, will require investment of around $216 million over the next three years to reach the planned annual production of one million tyres.
- The Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) warned against possible social conflicts this year resulting mainly from the heavy tax burden and low real wages.
NARODNA OBRODA - President Michal Kovac said Slovak defence costs without integration into NATO would be significantly higher than the expenditures required for joining the alliance.
- The Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said the central bank expected a further short-term increase in interbank interest rates.
- The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) posted turnover of some 113 billion crowns last year, of which 98.3 billion crowns was accounted for by direct trades.
- According to preliminary calculations, state-run Slovak Railways broke even last year.
SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - The government holds its regular session today. The preliminary agenda does not include any major economic items.
